story: Acadia is granite that ice rearranged. The rock cooled from magma more than four hundred million years ago; the Laurentide ice sheet then ground across Mount Desert Island, rounding its summits, gouging out the trough that holds Somes Sound and leaving boulders stranded where the ice let go of them — Bubble Rock still sits on its ledge above Jordan Pond, a long way from the outcrop it came from.

Because the island was scraped rather than buried, its soils are thin and its edges abrupt, and that makes for a lot of habitats in a small space. Spruce and fir hold the cold, wet headlands; northern hardwoods take the sheltered slopes; the intertidal rock between the tide marks carries a band of life that changes every few feet of height. A fire in 1947 burned across more than ten thousand acres on the island's eastern side, and the birch and aspen that came back after it still mark the burn's edge in autumn colour.

The Wabanaki have summered on this coast for thousands of years. Painters of the Hudson River School arrived in the 1840s and their canvases brought the first wave of summer visitors; the wealthy followed, and then — unusually — gave much of the land away. Charles Eliot and George B. Dorr assembled it through a public trust, and it became a national monument in 1916 and the first national park east of the Mississippi in 1919.

John D. Rockefeller Jr spent nearly three decades laying out forty-five miles of broken-stone carriage road through the park, with seventeen hand-cut bridges and no cars on any of it. They are still closed to cars, and they are the best way to see the interior.

sightNotes.poi-acadia-cadillac-mountain: The highest headland on the eastern seaboard, and among the first places in the United States to catch the sunrise.
sightNotes.poi-acadia-jordan-pond: A glacial tarn below the twin summits of the Bubbles, circled by a level shore path.
sightNotes.poi-acadia-thunder-hole: A narrow inlet where an incoming swell slams air out of a sea cave with a boom.
sightNotes.poi-acadia-sand-beach: A pocket of shell sand between granite headlands, in water that rarely passes 55°F.
sightNotes.poi-acadia-otter-cliff: A 110-foot granite wall dropping straight into the Atlantic.
sightNotes.poi-acadia-bass-harbor-head-light: An 1858 light station on the island's quiet south-western shore.
sightNotes.poi-acadia-schoodic-point: The park's mainland section, where dark basalt dykes cut through pink granite ledges.
sightNotes.poi-acadia-park-loop-road: Twenty-seven miles threading the eastern side of Mount Desert Island, designed to reveal the coast a view at a time.

entrances: Hulls Cove Visitor Center, north of Bar Harbor — the usual first stop
Park Loop Road fee station, on the island's eastern side
Schoodic Peninsula, on the mainland, reached from Winter Harbor
Isle au Haut, by mail boat from Stonington
planYourVisit.reservations: The park has no entry reservation, but driving the Cadillac Summit Road requires a separate vehicle reservation, released in advance and again on a rolling short-notice window. The free Island Explorer shuttle runs in season and needs none.
permits: Backcountry camping is not permitted anywhere in the park
Lobster and crab fishing within park waters follow state licensing
camping: Blackwoods Campground, near Bar Harbor, reservable
Seawall Campground, on the quiet side of the island
Schoodic Woods Campground, on the mainland
Duck Harbor Campground, five lean-tos on Isle au Haut, by permit
lodging: Bar Harbor, Northeast Harbor and Southwest Harbor
seasonalClosures: Most of the Park Loop Road closes from December to mid-April
Cadillac Summit Road closes for the winter
The Precipice, Jordan Cliffs and Valley Cove trails close in spring and summer while peregrine falcons nest

chronology.text: Magma cools underground to form the granite the island is made of.
The retreating ice sheet leaves rounded summits and the trough of Somes Sound.
Samuel de Champlain charts the island and names it Isle des Monts Déserts.
Hudson River School painters draw the first summer visitors to the coast.
Charles Eliot and George B. Dorr form a trust to hold island land for the public.
John D. Rockefeller Jr begins the carriage-road system, eventually forty-five miles of it.
Sieur de Monts National Monument is proclaimed.
It becomes Lafayette National Park, the first national park east of the Mississippi.
A fire burns more than ten thousand acres on the island's eastern side.

safety: The tide cuts people off. The Bar Island land bridge and the ledges at Ship Harbor and Wonderland are walkable for only a few hours either side of low water — carry a tide table and watch the clock.
Granite ledges are slick when wet or frosted, and the surf at Thunder Hole and Schoodic Point has swept people off rock that looked a safe distance from the water.
The Precipice, Beehive and Jordan Cliffs trails climb iron rungs and ladders on exposed cliff. They are not for anyone uneasy with heights, and they are dangerous in ice.
regulations: Drones may not be launched, landed or flown in the park.
Dogs are welcome on most trails and all carriage roads on a six-foot leash, but not on the ladder trails, in the Duck Harbor campground or on Sand Beach in season.
Bicycles belong on the carriage roads and paved roads, never on hiking trails.

fees.title: Timed entry reservation - location
fees.detail: Vehicle reservations are not required for any other areas of the park, or for visitors who enter the area by foot, bike, or taxi. Vehicle reservations provide a timed entry, but do not require a departure time until 9 pm, when the road closes to vehicles. Reservations do not permit re-entry. Reservations are per vehicle, not per person. Reservations do not assign a specific parking space. Parking is prohibited outside of designated spaces. Cadillac is not served by the Island Explorer bus system.

fees.title: Private vehicle
fees.detail: Valid for seven days. Admits private, non-commercial vehicle (15 passenger capacity or less) and all occupants. This includes rental cars, RVs, and vans with fewer than 16 passengers. If the vehicle pass is purchased, no other pass is necessary.

fees.title: Motorcycle
fees.detail: Valid for 7 days. Admits up to 2 private, non-commercial motorcycles with up to 4 total passengers.

fees.title: Per person
fees.detail: Valid for seven days. Admits one individual with no car (bicyclist, hiker, pedestrian). Youth 15 and under are admitted free of charge.

fees.title: Education/academic groups
fees.detail: School groups and other academic institutions may qualify for an Educational Fee Waiver. If not qualified, please check fees for large or commercial groups.

fees.title: Nonresident
fees.detail: Each non-US resident aged 16 and older visiting Acadia National Park must pay a $100 nonresident fee (in addition to the standard entrance fee), unless they are admitted with an Annual or America the Beautiful Pass. This includes nonresidents entering as part of a commercial tour group, commercial use authorization (CUA) group, or concessioner tour group.

operatingHours: Acadia National Park is open year-round. Check our website for park facilities operating hours, such as Hulls Cove Visitor Center.
weather: Located on Mount Desert Island in Maine, Acadia experiences all four seasons. Summer temperatures range from 45-90F (7-30C). Fall temperatures range from 30-70F (-1-21C). Typically the first frost is in mid-October and first snowfall begins in November and can continue through April with an average accumulation of 73 inches (185 cm). Winter temperatures range from 14-35F (-10 - 2C). Spring temperatures range from 30-70F (-1-21C).
directions: From Boston take I-95 north to Augusta, Maine, then Route 3 east to Ellsworth, and on to Mount Desert Island. For an alternate route, continue on I-95 north to Bangor, Maine, then take I-395 to U.S. Route 1A east to Ellsworth. In Ellsworth, take Route 3 to Mount Desert Island.
